subject: Tier oscillation & feature-bundle swap request — Brightline Labs
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightline.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Help — need a clear path between Pro and Burst tiers for spikes

Hi Michael,

Quick note from Brightline Ops — we had a couple of unexpected traffic spikes this week (attached usage_report_May.csv) and our costs briefly doubled when the service scaled into the Burst tier. We want to avoid surprise bills but also need the ability to handle these short bursts.

Can you outline the options to: 1) temporarily add burst capacity for predictable cost, 2) perform a short downgrade to a lower tier but keep a few features (embeddings & prefix caching), or 3) enable an autoscale buffer that triggers credits instead of full-rate throughput?

Our renewal is 2026-08-01 so we prefer a short-term arrangement (6–8 weeks) if possible — we can revisit at renewal. Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call this week.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform
Brightline Labs

Attachment: usage_report_May.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Help — need a clear path between Pro and Burst tiers for spikes

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the data, that helps. Short answer: we can offer a few pragmatic paths depending on what you prioritize (cost predictability vs. burst headroom vs. preserving features).

Outlined options (high level):

1) Surge credit + transient Burst add-on (recommended for short spikes)
   - Add a "flex-burst" add-on for a fixed window (e.g., 6–8 weeks).
   - Redwood issues usage credits to neutralize the variable portion above an agreed baseline.
   - Can be combined with rate-limiting knobs to cap peak spend.

2) Stepwise downgrade + feature bundle (cost-first)
   - Downgrade from Pro -> Standard for N months but carry a "feature bundle" that preserves embeddings + prefix caching + limited KV cache.
   - Feature bundle is an add-on SKU and can be prorated on billing cycle.

3) Autoscale buffer with metered credits (engineering approach)
   - We enable an autoscale buffer to absorb small spikes; any overage converts to discounted metered usage with credits applied automatically.

Ask: can you confirm typical spike magnitude (peak qps or token/sec), and how long spikes last on average? That will determine which option is most cost-effective.

If you like, Ben can run a quick cost-sim for options 1 vs 2 with proration numbers. I attached a short PDF with the three options and a ballpark for a 6-week window.

Open to a call today after 2pm PT or tomorrow morning.

—Michael
Michael Grant

Alyssa — quick note from my side: option 1 (flex-burst + surge credits) is usually easiest to stand up and keeps you on Pro feature parity.

Proposal: 3-month flex-burst add-on, billed monthly, with a 20% pilot discount on the add-on for the first two months. Canary rollback: if spend > threshold we auto-switch to a negotiated cap and issue credits retroactively for the overage.

Two questions for procurement:
- Can Brightline confirm acceptable monthly cap (USD) for the pilot?
- Do you need a formal amendment or a short-term PO?

Happy to join a call to walk the numbers.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Looping in the ops/legal side so we can move fast. Quick notes on proration and billing mechanics (from policy):

- Add-on proration: any add-on added mid-cycle is prorated by days remaining in the billing cycle. We can apply credits to the next invoice if needed.
- Downgrade protections: if a customer downgrades within 30 days, we allow a one-time credit exchange (subject to usage reconciliation).
- Amendment: I'll draft a 2-month flex-burst amendment (BRI-2345 amendment) that contains the pilot discount and the emergency cap clause. I put a draft in the attachment — please review.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alyssa confirms desired monthly cap and whether procurement prefers an amendment or PO.
2) We finalize amendment and send for e-sign (DocuSign).
3) Engineering will enable the quantization flag in a trial pod (if requested) and we’ll log the feature enablement in the amendment.

Link: https://redwood.app/docusign/amend/BRI-2345

Thanks — I’ll stand by to update the draft once we get the cap.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks all — appreciate the fast turn. Brightline is happy to proceed with option 1 (flex-burst add-on) for a two-month pilot (June–July) with the 20% pilot discount on the add-on. We propose a soft monthly cap of $18,000; please send the final amendment for signature.

A couple of items to include explicitly in the amendment:
- Quantization feature enabled in trial pods for the pilot window (we want to test cost/latency gains)
- Canary rollback condition and the exact language on retroactive credits
- Statement of baseline throughput and how credits are calculated (we’ll share our 95th percentile baseline after you confirm the cap)

If you can get a DocuSign to procurement today, we’ll aim to sign by EOD tomorrow. Call if easier.
